bibliography.citation: Langdon, Stephen H. The Epic of Gilgamish, PBS 10/3 (1917).
Jastrow, Morris Jr., and Albert T. Clay. An Old Babylonian Version of the Gilgamesh Epic (1920).
George, Andrew R. The Babylonian Gilgamesh Epic: Introduction, Critical Edition and Cuneiform Texts (2003), pp. 172-192 and pls. 1-3 as reported by eBL.
Electronic Babylonian Literature, Poem of Gilgameš, Old Babylonian II manuscript record, live state checked 2026-08-22.

composite_layer.relationship: The tablet is one physical witness represented in modern composite and synoptic routes. Neither the Penn/CDLI Q-label nor the eBL chapter makes the tablet identical to a reconstructed composition, fixed reading, translation, or complete Old Babylonian poem.

find_context.documentation_limit: The conflicting provider statements were not reconciled by excavation documentation. None is promoted to an exact findspot, composition place, scribal school, or ancient circulation route.
find_context.source_note: Penn reports Iraq, Warka (uncertain), while its description preserves a CBS Register note naming Sippar. CDLI reports Nippur; eBL reports the broader Babylonia label.

path_identity.note: The path follows the stable Penn Museum CBS 07771 repository identity and intentionally uses uncertain because Penn, the CBS register note, CDLI, and eBL do not report one reconciled locality.

scholarly_classification.genre: Akkadian literary tablet; Old Babylonian Gilgamesh witness

visual_layers.rights_note: Penn excludes images from its CC BY 4.0 metadata dataset and provides a separate publication-permission route; no photograph was acquired.
CDLI links or renders scholarly line art under source-specific contributor terms; no drawing was acquired or authorized for publication.
